excerpts.paraphrase: The 2026/27 edition of the Laws of the Game applies from 1 July 2026.
Law 1 sets the touchline length between a minimum of 90 m and a maximum of 120 m.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.59
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 3: a match cannot start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.59
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 3: official competitions may use up to five substitutes, a number set by FIFA, the confederation or the national association.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.59
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 3: where five substitutes are allowed, each team gets at most three substitution opportunities.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.61
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 3 procedure: the player being replaced must be off the field within ten seconds of the substitution board, barring safety or injury.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.97
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 8: at a kick-off the opponents of the kicking team stay at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball until it is in play.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.98
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 8: at a dropped ball all other players of both teams stay at least 4 m (4.5 yds) from the ball until it is in play.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.98
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 8: outside the penalty area the ball is dropped for the team that would have kept or gained possession, including from a restart, if the referee can tell.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.101
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 9: the ball is out of play when it has wholly passed over the goal line or touchline, on the ground or in the air.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.103
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 10: a goal needs the whole ball over the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar, with no offence by the scoring team.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.115
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 12: an offence that involves contact is penalised by a direct free kick.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.115
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 12: excessive force (more than needed, or endangering safety) means a sending-off; reckless means a caution; careless needs no card.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.116
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 12: not every touch of the ball by a hand or arm is an offence.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.116
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 12: it is a handball offence if the hand or arm touches the ball after making the body unnaturally bigger.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.132
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 13: until the free kick is in play opponents must be at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball, with a goal-line exception.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.132
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 13: against a wall of three or more defenders, attackers must stay at least 1 m (1 yd) away until the ball is in play.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.135
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 14: other players must be at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the penalty mark, behind it and outside the area.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.135
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 14: when the ball is kicked the goalkeeper needs part of one foot on, level with or behind the goal line.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.136
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 14: if the kicker accidentally touches the ball twice and it does not enter the goal, an indirect free kick is awarded.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.141
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 15: opponents stand at least 2 m (2 yds) from the point on the touchline where the throw-in is taken.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.141
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 15: no goal can be scored directly from a throw-in; into the opponents' goal means a goal kick.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.142
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 15: after a visual five-second countdown for delay, a throw-in not taken is awarded to the opposing team.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.145
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 16: after a visual five-second countdown for delay, a goal kick not taken gives the opposing team a corner.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.145
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 16: opponents must be outside the penalty area until the goal kick is in play.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.149
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 17: a corner is awarded when the referee penalises a goalkeeper for controlling the ball with hands or arms for more than eight seconds.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.149
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 17: opponents must stay at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the corner arc until the ball is in play.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.77
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 5.4: a VAR may help only after a clear and obvious error or serious missed incident, within a short list of decision types.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.154
excerpts.paraphrase: VAR protocol: the referee may receive VAR assistance in five categories of decision or incident.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.77
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 5.4: a clearly incorrect corner-kick award can be reviewed if it can be fixed at once without delaying the restart; a competition option.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.73
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 5.2: competitions may use technology for offside, including semi-automated offside technology (SAOT).

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.73
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 5.2: the referee's decisions on facts connected with play, including whether a goal is scored, are final.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.26
excerpts.paraphrase: Throw-in and goal-kick countdown protocol: the referee visually counts down from five seconds with a raised hand.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.22
excerpts.paraphrase: Time-limited substitution protocol: after a late exit the substitute enters only at the first stoppage after one minute of running clock has passed since the restart.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.86
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 6.1: assistant referees indicate when a player in an offside position may be penalised.

excerpts.locator: IFAB Laws of the Game 2026/27 PDF p.85
excerpts.paraphrase: Law 6: other match officials (assistant referees, fourth official, VAR, assistant VAR and others) assist; the referee takes the final decision.

excerpts.paraphrase: 2026/27 change: a five-second visual countdown for delayed throw-ins; if exceeded, the throw-in goes to the opposing team.
2026/27 change: a five-second visual countdown for delayed goal kicks; if exceeded, a corner goes to the opposing team.
2026/27 change: a player treated on the field or causing an injury stoppage must leave for one minute after the restart, barring exceptions.
2026/27 change: no caution for a DOGSO offence if advantage is played and a goal is scored.

title: IFAB Law 11: Offside (Laws of the Game 2026/27)

license.name: IFAB copyright, no reproduction without permission

automated_access.note: Fetched with curl on 2026-11-27, HTTP 200; terms of use not read

derivative.note: Paraphrase with attribution and short quotes only

notes: Current-edition web text of Law 11, matched against the PDF pp.109-112 on 2026-11-27. No publication date on the page, so recency is the as_of date.

excerpts.paraphrase: Being in an offside position is not itself an offence.
A player is in an offside position if any part of head, body or feet is in the opponents' half and nearer their goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent.
Being level with the second-last opponent, or with the last two opponents, is not an offside position.
Hands and arms of all players, goalkeepers included, are not considered; the arm's upper boundary is the bottom of the armpit.
A player in an offside position when a team-mate plays or touches the ball is penalised only on becoming involved in active play.
The first point of contact of the play or touch is used, except when the goalkeeper throws the ball, where the last point of contact is used.
Gaining an advantage includes playing the ball after a rebound or deflection off a post, crossbar, match official or opponent, or after a deliberate save by an opponent.
A ball received from an opponent who deliberately played it, even by handball, gives no advantage unless it was a deliberate save.
No offside offence arises when a player receives the ball directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.
An offside offence is punished by an indirect free kick where it occurred, even in the player's own half.

title: IFAB Video Assistant Referee (VAR) protocol (2026/27)

license.name: IFAB copyright, no reproduction without permission

automated_access.note: Fetched with curl on 2026-11-27, HTTP 200; terms of use not read

derivative.note: Paraphrase with attribution and short quotes only

notes: Web page shows tracked 2026/27 changes (old and new wording together), so lessons should quote the clean PDF text (pp.153-158) for category counts. No publication date, so recency is the as_of date.

excerpts.paraphrase: The referee's original decision changes only if the review clearly shows a clear and obvious error.
Only the referee starts a review; the VAR and other officials can only recommend one.
Reviews have no time limit because accuracy matters more than speed.
The referee must always make a decision first; allowing play to continue can later be reviewed.
For subjective decisions such as foul intensity, offside interference or handball an on-field review is appropriate.
For factual decisions such as offside position, point of contact, location or ball out of play a VAR-only review is usually appropriate.
Once play has restarted, review is allowed only for mistaken identity or for violent conduct, spitting, biting or extremely offensive acts.
FAQ: VAR can step in on a clearly incorrect second yellow that leads to a red, not on a missed potential second yellow.
The VAR checks every situation automatically, so players and coaches need not and cannot request a review.
